intro.title: ::before and ::after
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage element with decorative icons and text labels using CSS pseudo-elements. You will learn the core concept of using ::before and ::after to insert content before or after an element's actual content, without modifying the HTML. The main technologies involved are CSS selectors and the content property. This technique allows you to add visual enhancements purely with CSS, keeping your HTML clean and semantic. By the end, you'll be able to create custom bullets, icons, and stylistic flourishes.
intro.usecase: The ::before and ::after pseudo-elements are essential for adding decorative or functional UI elements without cluttering your HTML. Developers use them to create custom icons for buttons in dashboards, add visual separators in navigation menus, or insert required field indicators in forms. For example, you might add a small arrow icon after a dropdown menu item or a subtle shadow before a modal panel to enhance depth. This technique keeps your markup clean while enabling rich, maintainable visual designs across components like filters, tooltips, and data panels.
